Semantic summary: entry 34-style battle-presentation sub-effect that moves the effect's source actor toward one fixed target party member (B5Context lookups keyed off the effect state's field 8 'actor' id and the first entry of its member-id array at field 0x24) using the same low-level Object_ResetMotion/Object_SetPosition/Object_SetMode(2) approach shape as set_approach_motion.c (scale 90, not that function's 80), sets snap_to_target/auto_face_motion, then runs 96 animation passes. Each pass reads the global 'facing' cursor twice (once at top of pass, once again after the frame-gated field writes, reusing the same cached value rather than re-reading the global), on frame 0 sets both objects' velocity_y/vertical_motion_strength for an initial launch, on frame 11 flips a sign field and nudges both objects' y by a per-actor amount from Func_080b5070, on frame 54 fires ObjectGroup_UpdateMembers and re-derives both objects' velocity_y/vertical_motion_strength/acceleration/speed_limit for a second, weaker motion phase, on frame 64 reverses the frame-11 adjustment and calls Object_SetMode(object,0), projects the source actor's live x/y/z through EffectPosition_ApplyBaseAndYOffset every pass and halves the resulting screen x, draws a single 32x64 flash sprite at frames 54-55, and for a 12-pass window (frames 56-67) draws a 16-point sine/cosine ring of 32x64 sprites around the projected position, selecting the sprite cel from the pass's position in that window.

The `(x + ((u32)x >> 31)) >> 1` bit-trick noted elsewhere in this family does appear once here (the ring-loop's `cel_phase / 2` cel-select division) and was left as a genuine `/2` per the family guidance, since it is a real signed halving over a value the compiler cannot prove non-negative at that point even though the enclosing `cel_phase >= 0 && cel_phase <= 11` guard establishes it dynamically; the *other* halving in this owner (`screen[0] >>= 1` on the projected x) compiles to a single bare `asrs` with no sign-correction pair and was written as a plain right shift accordingly, not a division.

Every `bl` target inside games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s's _call_via_rN trampoline bundle was modeled as a real indirect call through the traced `draw` (DrawRectangleFn) value read from heap_cache[7], per this family's already-established Func_080072f4/Func_080072f8 finding -- no fictional Func_080072f4/Func_080072f8 prototypes were declared.

Field 0x1C on struct MotionObject (the sign-toggled sync flag at frames 11/64) falls inside motion_object.h's still-unnamed `unknown_14[0x10]` span; it was accessed with a raw M2C_FIELD rather than extending the shared header, since only this one owner's evidence is available for it so far.
